senses.sense_definition: The purchase of something before it is made available or offered for sale to others.

examples.text: The company secured its supply through the <w>preemption</w> of raw materials before competitors could bid.
Investors exercised their right of <w>preemption</w> to acquire new company shares ahead of the public.

senses.sense_definition: The supersession or invalidation of a lower jurisdiction's law by an overlapping law from a higher authority.

examples.text: Federal <w>preemption</w> prevents individual states from setting conflicting airline safety standards.
The court ruling relied heavily on federal <w>preemption</w> to dismiss the local regulations.

senses.sense_definition: The temporary interruption of a computer task by the operating system with the intention of resuming it later.

examples.text: Thread <w>preemption</w> allows the processor to switch quickly between different active applications.
Without proper <w>preemption</w>, an unresponsive program could freeze the entire operating system.

senses.sense_definition: The legal right or act of purchasing public land by a settler who has already settled on it.

examples.text: Under the new statute, squatter <w>preemption</w> gave homesteaders legal priority over absentee speculators.
Early settlers claimed their property through frontier <w>preemption</w> after clearing and farming the plots.

senses.sense_definition: A township and census-designated place in Mercer County, Illinois, United States.

examples.text: They bought a small farm outside <w>Preemption</w> and lived there quietly for decades.
The quiet community of <w>Preemption</w> is situated in northwestern Illinois.
